name: Khan Academy
line: Khan Academy teaches by course: videos, then exercises. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review happen at every problem.
description: AMP vs Khan Academy: Khan teaches by course, with videos, exercises and tests. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous, at every problem.
verdict: Khan Academy teaches through courses of videos, articles and exercises, and a skill's level moves with exercises, quizzes and tests [1][2]. At home, the parent or the learner chooses what to work on [3]. In AMP, assessment is continuous: every answer updates the learner's level and sets the next problem, and each problem carries its own hint, lesson and worked answer.

reasons.title: Continuous assessment
reasons.body: AMP has no separate test and no test day. Every answer updates the learner's level in that part of math and sets the next problem: new work within reach, a gap to close, or an old skill due back. In Khan Academy, a skill's level moves with exercises, quizzes, unit tests and Course Challenges [2]. The next piece of work is chosen by the adult or the learner. At home, Khan's guide asks the parent to choose courses, set a routine and make assignments [3]. In classrooms on Khan's new experience, the teacher assigns Missions [4].

reasons.title: The problem is the unit
reasons.body: In AMP, everything hangs off the problem: a hint that gives the first step, a lesson with a worked example, a film where there is one, the worked answer afterward, and links to the skills it builds on and leads to. Khan Academy is organized by course. A course is split into units, and units into lessons of videos, articles and exercises [1][3]. A learner watches a video or reads an article, then practices [5][6]. A meta-analysis of 55 studies found that worked examples improve math performance [7].

reasons.title: Feedback on every answer
reasons.body: After each problem AMP shows whether it was right, the correct answer and the worked steps. Khan Academy exercises give hints and instant feedback [5][6]. Where Khanmigo, Khan's AI tutor, is turned on, it sits on content pages and guides with questions instead of giving answers [8][9]. In a two-year trial, Khanmigo's help was one message away, and the median student messaged it in 17% of the exercise sessions in which they made a mistake [10]. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, in a mix of ages and subjects, feedback that explains had the largest average effect [11].

reasons.title: Continuous review
reasons.body: In AMP, learned skills come back in ordinary practice, at growing intervals, mixed with other math. Khan Academy's quizzes, unit tests and Course Challenges mix skills [2]. In Classic Khan Academy, review of earlier skills is the Mastery Challenge: a short mixed set that the learner starts [12]. Cathy Duffy's review says there is no cumulative review within units until the final exam [5]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% on the researchers' own test a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [13].

reasons.title: Moving on, and going back
reasons.body: In AMP a learner shows a skill by getting it right without help, more than once, and moves on. Repeated misses send practice back to what the skill builds on. Khan Academy's Readiness Check finds gaps from earlier grades and adds practice on them before related grade-level work [14][15]. A teacher assigns it, and only in US partner districts [16]. A learner working outside a class uses Khan's Classic experience, where recommended lessons may appear after an activity [4][1]. We found no step back to earlier skills after repeated misses in the pages we read there.

rows.range: Pre-K through multivariable calculus, in separate courses [17].
rows.start: The adult picks the course. A Course Challenge, a test over the whole course, can find gaps [3]. In US partner districts, a teacher can assign a Readiness Check [16].
rows.teaching: Short videos and articles, then exercises with hints and instant feedback [5][6]. Where turned on, Khanmigo, an AI tutor, guides with questions on content pages [8][9].
rows.next: At home, the learner or the parent chooses [3]. In classrooms on the new experience, teachers assign Missions [4].
rows.mastery: Proficient: every question right on an exercise, and one miss can be erased by a bonus question. Mastered: right again on a later mixed-skill assessment [2][18].
rows.review: Mastery Challenges: short mixed sets on earlier skills, started by the learner [12].
rows.print: No printable math practice found in its help center. Its printables are a progress tracker and motivational pages [19][3].
rows.adult: Khan's homeschool guide asks the parent to choose content, set a routine, make assignments, monitor reports and offer guidance [3].
rows.reports: Activity by course, a report for each learner, and assignment scores [20].
rows.evidence: Randomized trials. A university-run two-year trial found about 0.06 to 0.08 SD a year [10]. No Evidence for ESSA rating [21].

theirs: Khan Academy is a library of math courses from pre-K through multivariable calculus [17]. Khan says it is best used as a supplement to regular schooling [22].

A course is split into units, and units into lessons of videos, articles and exercises [1][3]. A learner watches a short video or reads an article, then practices with hints and instant feedback [5][6]. Exercises, quizzes, unit tests and Course Challenges move each skill up or down a level, and a later mixed-skill assessment can raise a skill to Mastered [2]. Where Khanmigo, Khan's AI tutor, is turned on, it sits on content pages and guides with questions [8][9]. At home, the parent chooses the courses, sets the routine and makes assignments [3].
credit: A high bar for Mastered. A skill must be right again on a later mixed-skill assessment, and misses there move it back down [2].
Short videos show a topic worked on a digital blackboard before a learner practices it [5].
Randomized trials, including one run by university researchers over two years in 18 Tennessee middle schools [10][23].

theirs: The largest recent trial ran for two years in 18 middle schools in Hamilton County, Tennessee, with about 6,900 students in daily intervention math [10][24]. University of Toronto researchers ran it with outside funders, and Khan staff advised on the platform and helped arrange the district partnership and data sharing [10]. Adding Khan Academy with Khanmigo raised math scores about 0.06 standard deviations a year across both years and 0.08 in the second, against grades that kept their usual remediation, often other math software. Year one alone showed no significant effect. The paper is a working paper, not yet peer reviewed, and the authors say the gains resemble what Khan practice without AI predicts [10].

In two other experiments, weekly coaching that helped teachers use Khan Academy for mastery practice raised scores 0.12 to 0.22 standard deviations, with the gains from classrooms averaging at least 35 minutes a week [23]. In government middle schools in India that all had Khan Academy, adding a dedicated on-site staff member to run it raised use from 7.2 to 47.4 minutes a week and math scores by almost half a standard deviation over 31 weeks [25]. Both trials compare added support with Khan Academy alone.

Khan Academy's own analyses of district use report larger gains for students who reached its recommended 30 minutes a week: about 5.5% of students in 2021-22, by our arithmetic, and about 9% in results published in November 2024 [26][27]. The 2021-22 brief says it cannot rule out self-selection [26]. Evidence for ESSA lists Khan Academy and Khanmigo without a rating ("No studies met inclusion requirements") [21][28]. We found no What Works Clearinghouse intervention report for either.
ours: Two findings bear most on this comparison. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% on the researchers' own test a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [13]. A meta-analysis of 40 studies of computer-based feedback, across a mix of ages and subjects, found the largest average effect for feedback that explains [11]. AMP applies both at every problem.

AMP's own outcome studies are planned: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. The research behind each part of AMP is in our report, and the code is public.

them: You want a learner to watch a short video on a topic, then practice it.
amp: You want every answer to set the next problem, with no one planning the course.
You want every answer followed by the worked steps.
You want learned skills to keep coming back in practice, without anyone starting a review.
Your learner is at different levels in different parts of math.
You want printed workbooks made from your child's own record, with worked answer keys.

questions.question: How is AMP different from Khan Academy?
questions.answer: In Khan Academy, a learner works through courses of videos, articles and exercises, and at home the parent or the learner chooses what comes next [1][3]. AMP has no separate test: every answer sets the next problem, each problem carries its own teaching, and learned skills return in ordinary practice.

questions.question: Does Khan Academy work?
questions.answer: In a two-year randomized trial in 18 Tennessee middle schools, adding Khan Academy with Khanmigo to daily intervention math raised scores about 0.06 to 0.08 standard deviations a year [10]. In two other trials, weekly coaching for teachers using Khan Academy raised scores 0.12 to 0.22 standard deviations, compared with Khan Academy without the coaching [23].

questions.question: Can a learner use both?
questions.answer: Yes. They are separate programs, and AMP places a learner from their own first answers, whatever else they use.
